<1>What happens.</1> The app lists the apps that are uninstalled on this phone, and in <2>Root</2> mode only those that still have a data folder, with its size. Each one is cleared with <3/>; if that is refused, Root removes the app's data folders directly, and without Root the app is brought back for you with <4/> and removed again <5>without</5> keeping its data. <1>What is not touched.</1> Your apps themselves, their data and settings, logins and accounts, saved games, photos, videos, downloads and every other file in your folders. Nothing is uninstalled and no app is reset.

<1>What is trimmed.</1> Only cache: the temporary files each app keeps in its own <2>cache</2> folder (and in its <3>code cache</3> folder), on the phone's internal storage and in the app's folder under Android/data. That is things like downloaded thumbnails and images, web pages a browser kept for next time, map tiles, video and music that was only buffered, and temporary files an app made while working. Android treats all of it as safe to throw away, and the app makes it again when it needs it.

<1>What it does.</1> <2/> asks Android to free space by deleting app caches until the phone has the amount of free storage you give it. 128 GB is more free space than any phone has, so the target can never be reached: Android keeps going and clears every cache it is allowed to clear, in every app, instead of stopping after the first few. The apps it starts with, and the order, are Android's own choice.
<1>What it runs.</1> The button runs <2/> on the phone, the same as typing <3/> on a computer. It needs a working mode (ADB, Wireless Debugging, Shizuku or Root); without one the button is locked.

Apps that are running right now may keep some of their cache until they close.
